d:
Be warned, members of the High Order have been seen in the vicinity of the standing stones north of the village. We have warned them time and again to not meddle at our sacred sites, but they are growing more bold in pushing us. Prove your resolve to us by going to the standing stones and dispersing them.
I am loathe to condone outright bloodshed, but do what you must to drive them off. Return to me when it's done.
p: Do what must be done, adventurer.
c:
Direct conflict with our shen'dorei brothers and sisters only weakens us as a people, but decisive action must at times be taken to prevent greater tragedy.
The mages of the High Order have zero regard for the consequences of their magical meddling. The forces that bind our island are fragile and vulnerable and all it could take is one thoughtless action to destroy our home.

d:
The recent emergence of the leylines on the surface of Zephras has been profound for our order. We have more direct and tangible access to the energies that permeate this place and it has increased our understanding of said magic greatly.
The Windshapers, however, view these emergences as scars on the land that must be "healed". This is an affront to our order and is something we simply cannot abide.
Go to the leyline in the forest to the southwest and drive off the Windshapers you find there.
c:
Sometimes I find it hard to distinguish between the blind zealotry of the Al'Aketh cult, and the stubborn refusal of the Windshapers to change.
If they truly believed the winds would guide us, they should be sensing the direction the winds are blowing and flow with them rather than against them.

d:
Greetings, young friend. I oftentimes come here to look upon the ancient anchor pylon. Gifts from the spirits of the winds, they bind and sustain our island. Of late however, their magic has grown unstable and inconsistent.
They suffer no distress I can see. Their splendor has not changed.
If you'd like, I can lend you my gift to look upon them yourself.
skyborne-male
p:
My gift is simple, and mundane. I cannot peer between worlds such as those with the skysight, nor can I draw upon the magic of the ley lines beneath Zephras like others can. But a gift it remains and I am grateful to have it.
Appreciation of what you have is the key to happiness. Yearning for what you may have, or what you have lost, only leads to despair.
c: Thank you for taking a moment to share this with me. I will continue to watch over the grove, and ponder on the state of our homeland.

d:
A key tenent of being an adventurer is the pursuit of divinity. This is not the pursuit of godhood, but merely the pursuit of good itself, for good's sake. We've all arrived at this place due to tragedy of one form or another, and it would be easy to lose that grace that defined us as adventurers in life.
Go to the Undercity and seek out Tanis Alderwood in the Trade Quarter. They are in need, and they could benefit greatly from some grace.
c: You... You are an adventurer? Please, do not hurt me. I-I know I'm not supposed to be panhandling. I have no quarrel with you or your order. Leave me be, I beg you!

d:
Wait, you want to... Help? Why would an adventurer want to help a beggar like me?
Well, I suppose that you could be of some assistance.
It's my wife you see. She, well... She's falling apart. I mean that literally. The apothecaries can stitch her back together right as rain, but they are about the Dark Lady's business and none are available to help. If you could perhaps bring me some fresh cloth then I could at least make her a wrapping to hold her together while we wait for the apothecaries.
p: I hope that this is no imposition upon you, goodly adventurer.
c: This is very kind of you, adventurer. Very kind indeed.

d: I don't know why you'd go out of your way to help me, but I appreciate it. If someone sent you my way, tell them I appreciate them too. You'll always have a friend in Tanis Alderwood, adventurer.
c:
You have done well, friend. It was a small thing, but even small acts of service such as this may help strengthen our connection to the light.
The Dark Lady and many in her service mistrust us. Some even conspire against us, but we will visit their skepticism and fear with courage and righteousness. We will show them that we are members of the Forsaken and we are willing to do our part, be it large or small, to help our people prosper once again.
Take this symbol, you will need it for what comes next.

d:
It's time to demonstrate your ability to channel one of the light's greatest gifts.
The item I just gave you is called the Symbol of Life. Take care, as it may cause you some discomfort to handle a talisman of the light such as this. The light may be anathema to the force that created us, but it is still our guide and ally. The pain reminds us of this.
Go see Deathguard Billmuth downstairs. He just arrived and he has petitioned us for aid. Show him and the Forsaken what a true adventurer can do.
c:
So you'll help me, then? Good, good. I'll admit I'm not proud of resorting to... Well, resorting to asking adventurers for aid. The priests waved me away and you might be my friend's only chance.
Please, help me.

d:
Falgan and I were sent on a mission to scout out scarlet activity in Venomweb Vale. We managed to sneak close enough to one of their camps to hear about new orders involving an attack on Brill. Before we could decide what to do next, I stepped on a twig and the noise alerted them to us.
Falgan yelled at me to run, so I ran. By the time I realized he wasn't with me, I was halfway to Brill. That brave idiot probably stayed behind to hold them off for me.
Please, find my friend and help him if you can.
c:
I'm... Back? And saved by an adventurer no less? I see you carry a Symbol of Life. I've not seen one of those since... Well, since before the war when Lordaeron was a very different place. I can only assume you are here to help. Billmuth and I were sent here to scout out the scarlet activity here, and we found out that they are planning some kind of attack.
If you would be willing to help more, there may yet be more that you can do to help the Forsaken.

d:
These Scarlet Crusaders often carry satchels with their deployment orders. We know an attack is coming, but if we can recover their orders, we can warn the rest of the Deathguard and prepare an ambush.
You are clearly an impressive adventurer. Kill these scarlet animals and retrieve a copy of their orders and bring them back to Deathguard Billmuth. He'll take it from there.
c:
Thank you for saving my friend, friend. I will take these plans back to my commander and we will give those crusaders a welcoming they won't forget.
I know that many among our people mistrust you adventurers, but it's clear to me that you are Forsaken through and through. I won't forget this, and I'll make sure others know of what you did here today.

d:
Please give my thanks to Danitha Morr and tell her that the rest of the Deathguard will hear about the service that the adventurers of Bandarion Keep performed for us.
You have a lot of promise as an adventurer, and I am proud to have those like you among the ranks of the Forsaken. Dark Lady watch over you, friend.
c:
The Symbol of Life is only able to be used by an adventurer who is ready to make use of one of the light's greatest blessings. I'm proud to count you among us, and I now bestow upon you the gift of redemption. With this you will be able to resurrect your fallen companions. Use this new boon wisely.
You have done well for both the Forsaken as well as the adventurers of Bandarion Keep. Any steps we can take to win the hearts and minds of our fellow Forsaken is well worth the effort. Go with the light, friend.

d:
It's been long since ye were last tested, friend. Ye've shown patience, aye -- but now it's time ye learned of chaos... Of destruction. Fire's call is loud, and if ye're ready to pay its price, it'll speak to ye.
Seek out Bruegs Kindleborn, far east in the mountains. He dwells in a cave above South Gate Outpost. He'll know if ye're truly ready.
c: Hmm... That elder sent ye, eh? Well, an adventurer's word is solid, so I'll not argue. That means ye're ready for the next sapta. The sapta of fire. I see it in yer eyes already -- the burnin', the hunger. Ye've tasted power, and now ye want more. But mind yerself, friend. Remember what the stone taught ye. Fire's easy to wield, but harder to master. Know when to hold back.

d:
Aye, ye've the strength to bear the totem o' fire, lad--but strength alone won't make ye ready.
Beyond the Valley o' Kings, in the crags of Loch Modan, lies a hidden path to one o' our sacred peaks. There, Braldir Ashmantle guards the Shrine o' the Dormant Flame.
Take this torch to him--it shows yer intent. Return it burnin' by the shrine's brazier, and I'll see ye earn the totem proper.
p:
Greetin's, friend. Ye've made it to the Shrine o' the Dormant Flame, eh? Not many do. Only those well-versed in the adventurer's path can grasp the secrets this place holds.
Shame ye came all this way just to be turned back--the climb's no stroll through Dun Morogh. But I'm the shrine's keeper, and I won't be lettin' just any foot trod about.
c:
Ah, me apologies, friend. Didn't spot the Torch in yer hand. An honor to meet ye proper.
Many a wanderer climbs these heights chasin' tales of treasure or beasts, only to find naught but stone and silence. But we know better, don't we, friend?
This shrine holds truths far deeper than the Alliance can fathom. To us, it's a sacred flame that waits to be awakened.

d:
Bah, ye didn't trek all this way for tales, did ye, friend? Ye seek the Eternal Flame and the fire totem.
First, ye'll need a sapta to bind yer spirit to the flame.
I'll craft it--but I'll need two things: fire tar from Tunnel Rat Geomancers in the kobold caves up north, and a reagent pouch from a Stonesplinter Seer lurkin' in the southern hills. Dangerous work, but worthy of the flame.
p: Aye, I've near all I need for the fire sapta, friend--just missin' the fire tar and the seer's pouch. The tar's carried by Tunnel Rat Geomancers in the kobold caves up north. The pouch ye'll need to wrest from a Stonesplinter seer in the southern hills. These ingredients are bound to flame, as all true saptas must be. Their elemental ties make our craft strong.
c:
These'll do fine, friend.
Fire ain't just fury and ruin--mark me words. It's life, it's forge, it's the breath o' creation. All things are bound in balance. One force tempers the other, gives it meaning. Without shadow, light's but a glare. Without flame, stone's but cold memory.
Masterin' magic means knowin' when to blend, not just burn. That's true wisdom, lad.

d:
The fire sapta's ready, friend. Now ye face the flame. Use it at the shrine, then climb to the peak. There, ye'll see the spirit--he'll not strike 'til ye do, but he'll know ye see him.
Strike fast, lad. The longer ye wait, the stronger he burns. When he falls, take his glowing embers and place 'em in the brazier. Light the torch and earn the fire's favor.
p:
The brazier stands about a third your height, with charred inscriptions along its smooth metal rails. The metal shows no signs of wear from the weather, and the bowl seated at the top of it feels cool to the touch.
Blackrock Mountain looms in the distance, in clear view to honor from this sacred place.
c:
A white hot flame ignites within the bowl as you place the ember within. You can feel the magical effects of the sapta coursing through your body and the fire dances rhythmically before you.
You place the top of the torch within the basin, and it immediately catches on fire. The smoke seems to drift towards the peak of the looming mountain.

d:
Torch firmly in hand, you turn away from the brazier and look out over Loch Modan. You feel an excitement tugging at your spirit as the wind picks up and forces the flame to dance violently.
You start off down the path back to Dun Morogh in search of Bruegs Kindleborn.
p: Aye, friend? What do ye have there?
c:
By Madoran's beard, yer spirit burns brighter than any torch I've laid eyes on, friend--and that's somethin' to be proud of.
Keep walkin' this path, and the elements'll bend to yer will. Our kin will come to ye for wisdom and guidance. So let me be the first to offer me hearty congratulations--and present ye with yer newest totem. Ye've earned it, flameborn.
Take this and remember, it is sacred.

d:
A moment if you will, friend. Are you headed towards Shadowgale Forest? There is a druid conclave there in a cave to the northeast. I have been waiting on word from them but their correspondence is long overdue.
With Ban'aethall in ruins and all the unrest lately I worry something dire may have happened. Please, if you are able, go seek out Elegael Thornpaw and put my mind at ease.
c:
Thank goodness our message got to Lotheluum. Wait, where are the rest of the reinforcements? Surely it is not just you they sent?
So the message did not get through. We are in dire straits indeed then.
It seems we must handle this on our own. Time is of the essence.

d:
If we are to save my fellows in the Nightclaw Den, I am going to need some ingredients for a poultice. The first and most important is a spindly moss called Lady's Tear. It typically grows on the base of the trees here in Shadowgale.
This moss secretes a sticky substance that acts as an antiseptic and is perfect for binding open wounds. I have gathered what little I can reach but I know there is more in this forest.
Go and be swift. We are going to need a lot if the injured I left behind still live.
p: Have you found the Lady's Tear?
c:
Elegael takes the sticky mound of moss from you with a weak smile.
Thank you, friend, you have done well. This is exactly what we need.

d:
The other ingredient I need for the poultice is feathers from the Shadowgale shrieklings that roam this forest. In their juvenile form, the shrieklings have insulative feathers which would be ideal to put over the moss. These feathers will prevent the antiseptic sap from drying out and will provide at least some protection against the elements.
Be warned, the shrieklings are normally docile but they have been incredibly hostile of late. Their large talons can easily disembowel you if you aren't careful.
p: It deeply saddens me to ask you to kill the young shrieklings, but with the rise in their aggression it is for the best. We can only handle so many emergencies at a time.
c: Thank you for these. I will be sure to use every feather so their sacrifice will not be in vain.

d:
The Al'Aketh Cultists ambushed us with no warning, though their motives remain a mystery to me. I knew these cultists had clouds between their ears, but I never imagined they would upset the delicate balance here on Zephras with such brutality. Go, slay as many as you can and take their heirlooms if they wear any.
These storm-cursed cultists don't deserve to be called shen'dorei. The beasts of the forest can have their bodies. Their ashes don't deserve the winds.
p: I will make the cult pay for every drop of druid blood they have spilled this day.
c:
Elegael looks down at the collection of bloodied heirlooms with distress.
So many young lives with so much potential now gone forever. Thank you for returning these, adventurer.
I will hold onto them for safekeeping until I am able to take them to the High Elder. There they can go back into the collection and await the next and perhaps more worthy generation to come of age.

d:
The reason for cultists' presence here still baffles me, but I smell a familiar scent over the bloodshed.
One of our circle druids, Haalien, disappeared months back. It appears he's thrown his sorry hide in with the cultists.
Show him what happens when he spills the blood of his kin! Take his head and return it to me.
p: Are our brethren's lives truly worth so little to you, Haalien?
c:
Thank you, friend. No matter how much rage I have within me, it would have been difficult to strike down my own cousin.
Do not mourn for him. His ignorance and malice has killed many innocents this day.

d:
I have finished the poultices. Quickly, take them to the druids in the cave, north just across the clearing. I know my brethren are in much more dire condition than I. They are likely too injured to heal their own wounds. There are so few of us shen'dorei druids that every life is precious.
Before you go, I have a selfish request. My mate, Jorel Windsinger was in dire condition when I left. Please, see to his wounds if he still lives.
c:
Elegael's face pales as you relay the fate of Jorel and the condition of the rest of the druids.
No... No! This is far worse than I had--
Elegael chokes back a sob and grits her teeth, letting out a pained snarl.
They will pay. They will ALL pay. Anyone who allies with the Al'Aketh will feel my wrath! This I swear.

d: Tucked behind one of Haalien's bracers is a note that's been slightly torn and bloodstained in your fight. It looks like it contains useful information about the cultist motivations for the attack on the druid den. Elegael would be interested in this intel.
c:
They were here for the pylon? But to what end? We were not the original reason for their attack?
They murdered my people because we were an inconvenience! I shall tear apart every cultist with my fangs! I will make sure none leave this place with their lives.
Go, swiftly! If the orders truly originated in Valanaar, it means it is likely a traitor hiding there. Give the missive to Lotheluum in Valanaar and tell him what has transpired.

d:
It would appear that there is a correspondent hiding somewhere in Valanaar feeding information to the cult. I am clearly in no shape to make the journey, but Lotheluum needs to know what transpired here.
He should also know the fate of those who are no longer with us. Thanks to your help I think we can handle the rest of the situation from here, though the damage has been done.
Please go swiftly, friend. I hope our paths will cross again someday. Until then, I have cultists to slay.
c:
Lotheluum wears a look of genuine terror as you recount the events from the druid den.
I--I'm sorry, friend. I need just a moment. There are no words I possess that can describe the loss.
This is grave news indeed. If this missive is not fabricated, then we indeed have at best an accomplice and at worst a traitor here in Valanaar. I will take this to the High Elder immediately! I will not let my fellows' sacrifice be in vain.

d:
Long has it been since ye were last tested, friend. Ye have shown patience thus far in yer studies, but the time has come for ye to learn about the purity of water.
Seek out Norric Lochthane in Loch Modan. He is along the north western edge o' the lake, south of Stonewrought Dam. Ye will find him there at his burrow hut. Good luck to ye, friend.
c: The wind's rushin' at yer back, the stone's firm beneath yer boots, and the fire in yer belly's burnin' bright. Aye, it's time ye learned the truth o' water's purity. Yer path's been long, but it's yer spirit that'll carry ye further still. Now, go on, take that first step. The mountain waits for no one.

d:
If there's one truth ye need to learn about water, it's this: water means rebirth. It carves stone, cleanses filth, and heals the weary -- but only when it's pure. Taint it, and it'll ruin all it touches.
If ye seek the water sapta, find Hervdana Saegrund in the Wetlands. Her family dwells in a cave beneath the southern falls.
Go on then, don't let the river outrun ye.
c:
Aye, I see it in yer eyes, dwarf. You're wonderin' what kind o' soul chooses to live out here, deep in the Wetlands, with Dark Iron scum lurkin' about and nary a guard in sight. Well, we all have our reasons, love.
But the real question is, what brings you to our home? Out here at the edge of the falls, I reckon we both know the answer to that.
Hervdana stretches out her arm, fingers catching mist spray from the waterfall.

d:
Ah, so ye've come seekin' the sapta, have ye? Well then, listen close, love. To find understandin' and earn the sapta, ye must seek water in its various forms. As ye gather the samples, keep yer eyes open. Watch the beasts that guard it, the land it nourishes, and how it changes lives.
We'll start simple: fill this skin at the base o' the falls, where the fresh meets the brackish. Go on now, and mind the marsh.
p: I'm nearly ready to send ye off on the rest o' yer tasks. But tell me, have ye filled the skin yet? The ocean brings life, aye--but it carries sediment, minerals, and energies far different from the snowmelt and springwater of the highlands. Where sea and spring meet, there's wisdom to be found.
c:
Glad ye managed to steer clear o' the Dark Iron. Shame they've crept so far north--makes ye wonder what dwarfkind could do if the clans ever stopped squabblin' and worked as one.
Still, the tides rise high when the moons are strong, and the seawater floods the marsh. It's here that we study our estuary water.
Thank ye for this sacred offering. It marks the beginning of your stage as a vessel--one who seeks the waters' wisdom.

d:
Aye, Redridge drinks deep from Lake Everstill, but by the time the waters tumble down Stonewatch Falls, somethin' has seeped in. The murlocs down there are big, twisted brutes. Not like the ones ye find here or in the Loch. Lucky for the townsfolk they keep to the base o' the falls.
Bring a sampling to me. I've a mind to find out if it's magic, venom, or somethin' worse that's taintin' the waters near that old fort.
p: The folk o' Lakeshire don't ken how good they've got it--fresh water flowin' right at their boots, keepin' their nets full, their crops green, and their coin purses jinglin'. Even when the kingdom's guard can barely spare a lad with a sword, they've got Everstill watchin' over 'em.
c:
Aye, this is good water, friend. The magic used by the shadowseers in the region must be changin' the murlocs. Nothin' but pure water, this be. Yer dedication to the task at hand and abilities to seek out that which is needed prove you're ready for the next stage of your journey.
One more sample is all I need to create the reagent needed for your sapta. Norric will be pleased as well.
